subject: Predeclared gates for arms T and U, written BEFORE either was pushed.
context: Arm S (world model survives death) returned 42 levels against a five-run family mean of 33.8 and the highest shipped-scorer mean this project has recorded (8.638). It is now taking real board draws in the daily rotation. Arm K taught us what happens next if we do not check: its first run was 44 and its byte-identical replicate returned 28.
shared_preconditions: All 25 games run and hold their full 7,920s slot.
Peak GPU KV cache usage strictly below 0.90.
ZERO tracebacks from tool_agent.py in the kernel log. Both arms carry a source change, so a crash is the main risk and any traceback is an automatic REJECT.

q38-deathmem-rerun-v1.change: NOTHING. Byte-identical replicate of arm S.
q38-deathmem-rerun-v1.purpose: Arm S is already taking board draws. This is the cheapest possible insurance against repeating the arm-K mistake: if arm S's 42 was a lucky draw the way arm K's 44 was, we want to know before it consumes many of the 36 remaining slots. It also yields arm S's OWN paired per-game level-diff sd, which the gate amendment requires before any variance claim about a config.
q38-deathmem-rerun-v1.what_it_would_falsify: Return at or below 34 (the family mean plus nothing) and arm S's 42 was substantially luck: drop it from the rotation and give the slots back to A-temp09. Return 40 or above and arm S is the first change since the context-window raise with two independent runs behind it, and it should take the majority of the remaining draws.
q38-deathmem-rerun-v1.prediction_recorded_in_advance: I expect 34 to 44. Given the family's single runs span 28 to 44, one replicate cannot settle this on its own; it can only catch a collapse. That is the point, and it is worth 2h15m of an idle GPU session.

q38-deathmem-topk100-v1.change: Arm S plus LOCAL_ANALYZER_TOP_K 20 -> 100. Verified single-variable against arm S: identical src tree hash, one differing line in setup_commands.json.
q38-deathmem-topk100-v1.purpose: A ROTATION CANDIDATE, not a science experiment. top_k 100 pooled +3.7 levels over two runs, a tie that leans positive and was never shown to be harmful; arm S is +8.2. The two touch unrelated mechanisms (sampler truncation and world-model persistence), so a combined config is a reasonable third horse. Under the 2026-08-24 rule it needs only a ~21% prior of beating arm S to deserve draws, and splitting draws across equal-mean configs costs exactly zero.
q38-deathmem-topk100-v1.explicitly_not_claimed: That this is better than arm S. A single 25-game run cannot show that: single runs of one identical config span 28 to 44 on this instrument. The board draws decide it, not the bench.
